title: China Dominates Asian Games Swimming Opener; India Chases First Medal
excerpt: China won six of seven golds on the first night of pool swimming at the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, while India's 12-member men's squad began its campaign in the 100m freestyle and 100m backstroke heats.
body:
• China won six of the seven swimming gold medals on the opening night of the 20th Asian Games in Nagoya, with Japan's Tomoyuki Matsushita taking the seventh in the men's 200m individual medley.
  • World-record holder Pan Zhanle captured the men's 100m freestyle crown, while Tang Qianting broke the Asian Games record twice in a single day in the women's 50m breaststroke.
  • Three Games records fell on day one, with Xu Jiayu and 13-year-old Yu Zidi also lowering the marks in their events.
  • India's 12-member men's squad opened its campaign in the 100m freestyle and 100m backstroke heats as the country chases a first-ever Asian Games swimming medal.

China's swimmers made a commanding start to the pool programme at the 20th Asian Games on Sunday, winning six of the seven gold medals decided on the opening night at the Tokyo Aquatics Centre and setting three Asian Games records in the process.

World-record holder Pan Zhanle delivered the headline performance of the evening in the men's 100m freestyle. Pan, who set the world record of 46.40 seconds at the Paris Olympics, touched first ahead of two South Koreans — Kim Youngbeom took silver and Hwang Sunwoo bronze — giving Korea its first medals of the Games, according to SwimSwam's live recap. Pan had cruised through the morning heats in 48.07, just six-hundredths ahead of Hwang.

Records fall across the programme

The night's most emphatic swim came from Tang Qianting in the women's 50m breaststroke. The Chinese star broke the Asian Games record in the morning heats with 29.50, then lowered it again in the final to 29.45 — just one-hundredth of a second outside her own Asian record of 29.44, set earlier this year. Japan's Satomi Suzuki, 35, took silver in 29.91 to become the first Japanese woman under 30 seconds and set a new Japanese record, while China's Yang Chang claimed bronze in 30.24.

Xu Jiayu dominated the men's 100m backstroke in 51.98, taking down his own Games record of 52.23 from Hangzhou 2023 and finishing just off his Asian record of 51.86. Japan's Hidekazu Takehara edged South Korea's Lee Juho by a single hundredth for silver, 53.93 to 53.94.

The opening event of the night produced the youngest champion: 13-year-old Yu Zidi won the women's 200m butterfly in 2:05.08, breaking Zhang Yufei's Games record of 2:05.57 and slicing more than half a second off her own career best. China's Chang Mohan took silver in 2:08.44, with Japan's Misa Okuzono third in 2:09.67.

Japan's lone gold of the night came in the men's 200m individual medley, where Tomoyuki Matsushita beat compatriot Yumeki Kojima, with China's Wang Shun taking bronze. China closed the session by winning the women's 4x100m freestyle relay in a Games record, ahead of Hong Kong and Japan. In the women's 1500m freestyle, Li Bingjie led a podium completed by Singapore's Gan Ching Hwee and Japan's Ichika Kajimoto.

India's campaign begins

India fielded a 12-man swimming squad in Nagoya — the country's largest in recent editions — with the opening day's heats in the men's 100m freestyle and 100m backstroke marking the start of its campaign. Akash Mani carried India's hopes in the 100m freestyle heats, while Rishabh Das and Utkarsh Patil contested the 100m backstroke. None of the Indian swimmers reached the 100m freestyle final, where the top eight qualifiers were led by Pan in 48.07.

The squad's leading medal hopes are concentrated later in the week. Srihari Nataraj, India's most decorated active swimmer, is entered in the 50m backstroke, with heats and the final scheduled for Monday. Sajan Prakash, the veteran butterfly specialist, races the 200m butterfly on the final day of the pool programme, September 25.

The medal drought India wants to end

India has never won a swimming medal at the Asian Games, a drought that has persisted across every edition of the continental meet. The Bridge, previewing the swimming programme, pinned India's hopes of ending that wait on Nataraj and Prakash — two swimmers with genuine finals pedigree at the Asian level.

The task is formidable. China and Japan have historically split the overwhelming majority of Asian Games swimming medals, and South Korea's emergence — with world-class sprinters in Hwang and Kim — has made the podium harder to reach. For India, a first swimming final of the week would itself be a milestone worth noting.

What to watch next

Monday's programme brings the men's 50m backstroke, 50m freestyle and 100m breaststroke finals, plus the men's 4x200m freestyle relay — with Nataraj's 50m backstroke the focal point for Indian fans. The pool competition runs through September 25, with Prakash's 200m butterfly closing India's individual campaign.

For the Indian diaspora, the swimming action is being broadcast on the Sony Sports Network in India, while Willow TV is carrying free Asian Games coverage across North America.
